answer: Difficulty-retargeting minting resists sybils: a new identity is minted only by solving a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty auto-retargets to keep the global minting rate constant. As a farm pushes more heads at once, aggregate hashrate rises and the target tightens, so each marginal identity costs more than the last — a curve from a lagoon-calm floor to a hard marble wall. A burst of k fakes meets the steepest, umber-dark difficulty and pays super-linearly; honest agents entering at the natural rate pay the baseline. Precondition: the retarget window reacts before the farm finishes.
